extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of crisis communication / corporate public relations (DoD Joint Course in Communication audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study analysis of corporate crisis communication strategies (Union Carbide/Bhopal) focusing on tactics, timing, stakeholder management, and media relations during a major industrial disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness / Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate communications staff strongly recommended the company be as open as possible with all the information they had at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page frames openness as a recommended tactic to build public trust and focus on the human cost. Openness can conflict with legal advice; however the account suggests openness is often perceived as the 'correct strategy' in large-scale tragedies (Kurzman, 1987). Failure to be open led to impressions of 'stonewalling.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding information to limit legal liability (anti-transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Information should be withheld that may possibly implicate or confirm the company's responsibility for the Bhopal leak and hence increase its potential legal liability." (attorneys' recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an alternative/legal-driven strategy that can protect against immediate legal exposure but may damage public perception. The text contrasts this with openness and shows how attorney-led withholding contributed to mixed impressions and delayed releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response strategy choice (Avoidance vs Attachment/Forgiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership was divided between attempting to distance itself from the events in Bhopal (Avoidance Strategy) and providing maximum information and direct support to victims (Attachment/Forgiveness Strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a strategy is a central criterion: avoidance focuses on limiting corporate culpability; attachment focuses on acknowledging moral responsibility and supporting victims. The report suggests attachment (accepting moral responsibility) was widely perceived as the correct approach, but execution matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of initial communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's first formal release regarding the Bhopal incident came one week after the tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely information is critical; delays create perceptions of stonewalling and reduce effectiveness. The one-week delay is cited as a major failure hampering public trust and media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and operate a Crisis Communication Response Team (on-call)
rubrics_metrics.description: A crisis communication team was established and instructed to conduct daily press briefings at a minimum. Failure to have a Crisis Communication Response Team (on-call) was a major factor in media perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having an on-call, adequately staffed crisis team is essential for handling volume and complexity of media inquiries. The lack of manpower to respond to the crisis magnitude undermined the intended attachment strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular press briefings / consistent media cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis communication team was instructed to conduct daily press briefings at a minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily briefings provide a predictable flow of information and can counter impressions of withholding. Consistency in cadence helps shape the narrative and respond to fast-moving media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership presence and visible commitment (executive on-site)
rubrics_metrics.description: Union Carbide CEO, Warren Anderson, felt it was important for him personally to go to Bhopal to demonstrate the commitment the company had to the rescue effort and to the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive presence can signal commitment and accountability; however, legal/political advice may counsel against it (e.g., risk of arrest or legal exposure). The CEO's trip and subsequent arrest exemplify both potential benefits and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate information flow and communications infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company experienced severe difficulties in getting accurate information from the plant in India (phone lines scarce); Union Carbide had no means of established communication with its plant in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable channels for getting and distributing accurate information (redundant communications, local liaison) are essential. Lack of infrastructure compounds delays and misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and manage conflicting stakeholder goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's efforts were hampered by the often conflicting interests of various stakeholders (Indian Government, company leadership, shareholders, consumer/environmental groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective crisis communication requires mapping stakeholders, anticipating conflicting goals (e.g., government's desire to shift blame), and planning tailored messaging/coordination to minimize mixed signals and legal/political fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message framing: human cost vs financial/legal focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Union Carbide's initial crisis communication strategy centered on the financial costs of the tragedy, limiting its legal/financial responsibility; communication staff intended to focus on the human cost of the accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing determines public reaction: emphasizing human cost supports empathy and reputational recovery, while focusing on financial/legal consequences can appear self-interested. The report suggests focusing on human consequences is generally the more effective public strategy in such tragedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and crisis planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Shrivastava notes lack of preparation in planning for a crisis which led to lack of available information and a perception the company was unsympathetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-crisis planning (playbooks, simulated exercises, designated on-call teams) reduces response time, ensures information availability, and helps maintain perceived empathy and competence when a crisis hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to media focus and narrative dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass media coverage focused on the drama of the initial event (85% of stories) rather than in-depth causes (15%); television focused on human tragedy images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators should anticipate media's preference for dramatic human elements and craft messages and visuals that both satisfy that demand and steer attention toward desired framing (causes, corporate response, safety measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance legal counsel with public relations objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate attorneys recommended withholding information to limit liability; communications staff recommended openness—this internal conflict shaped the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear decision process to balance legal risk and reputational needs is necessary. Integrating legal and PR perspectives early (joint protocols) can prevent paralysis and mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for host-nation or partner organization's communication goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Union Carbide failed to account for the fact that the Government of India might have substantially different communication goals (to shift blame, demonstrate its handling of the disaster).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operating across jurisdictions, anticipate differing objectives of governments and local authorities; coordinate messaging and negotiation to avoid being blindsided by conflicting public narratives and actions (e.g., arrests, blame-shifting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource adequacy (manpower to respond to inquiry volume)
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication staff was quickly overwhelmed by the complexity of the issue and the number of media inquiries; they lacked the manpower to respond to a crisis of this magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale staffing and logistical support to the potential media and stakeholder response; under-resourcing leads to delays, inconsistent responses, and negative perceptions.
